stages.name: Inheritance and wealth inequality
stages.title: Inheritance and wealth inequality
stages.sub: Explain how passing wealth down the generations causes wealth inequality to persist.

steps.q: Wealth is the stock of assets someone owns, like property, savings and shares. When a wealthy person dies, do their house, savings and shares vanish?
steps.right: No, they get passed on to someone
steps.wrong: Yes, they disappear with the person
steps.hint: Think of a family home. Does it stop existing when the owner dies?

steps.q: Two children are both born today. One inherits a paid-off house and a share portfolio, the other inherits nothing. Did either child do anything yet to deserve this difference?
steps.right: No, neither has done anything yet
steps.wrong: Yes, the richer one worked harder as a baby
steps.hint: Both children are newborns. Can a newborn have earned anything?

steps.q: The child with the house and shares can use them as security to borrow cheaply, invest, and avoid rent. Will their wealth tend to grow faster than the child who started with nothing?
steps.right: Yes, it tends to grow faster
steps.wrong: No, both grow at the same rate

steps.q: Now imagine this repeating every generation: those with inherited assets pass on even more, those without inherit nothing to pass on. Does the wealth gap between the two family lines tend to narrow over time or widen?
steps.right: It tends to widen across generations
steps.wrong: It tends to narrow across generations
